simple.meaning: רַעַם (raʻam) is a Hebrew word meaning “a peal of thunder.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: רַעַם (H7482) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 26:14, with occurrences in Job, Psalms, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רַעַם (H7482) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in רַעַם (H7482) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: רַעַם (raʻam) / H7482 is traced through Job 26:14, Job 39:25, Psalms 77:19, Psalms 81:8 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways.

timeline.evidenceText: Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways.
As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’
Your way was through the sea;
“Hear, my people, and I will testify to you,
She will be visited by Yahweh of Armies with thunder, with earthquake, with great noise, with whirlwind and storm, and with the flame of a devouring fire.

definitions.full: H7482. raam רַ֫עַם noun [masculine] thunder ; — ascribed to ׳ר י ׳׃ absolute Isa 29:6 , רַ֑עַם בְּסֵתֶר Psa 81:8 (Baer Gi; i.e. thunder-cloud); suffix רַעַמְךָ קוֺל 77:19 ; 104:7 ; construct גבורתו רַעַם Job 26:14 (figurative of ׳י s display of might; opposed to שֵׁמֶץ ); figurative of captains, ׳ר שָׂרִים 39:25 , i.e. thunderous shouting ( + תְּרוּעָה ).
